job.title: Anatomical Pathologist
job.description:
Anatomical Pathologist

The role entails the responsibility of overseeing various operational laboratory activities, which includes coordinating and providing scientific and technical training, continuously reviewing and developing laboratory practices, ensuring adherence to operational standards and procedures, maintaining quality standards, and driving continuous process improvement.
 
Responsibilities

  • Possess a Bachelor's degree or higher in Science/Medical Laboratory Science or an equivalent qualification from a recognized tertiary institution, with relevant subjects related to pathology.
  • Show demonstrated knowledge and experience in delivering pathology services specific to the laboratory, including proficiency in using Laboratory Information Systems, Patient Systems, Quality Control Systems, and computer programs like Microsoft Office suite.
  • Exhibit a customer-focused approach, demonstrating strong interpersonal skills, effective oral and written communication skills, and the ability to communicate proficiently with customers, patients, clinical and laboratory staff. This includes report writing skills, statistical evaluation of scientific data, and the ability to effectively communicate policies and procedures.
  • Demonstrate the ability to work responsibly and efficiently, managing competing priorities to meet deadlines.
  • Display the ability to work both collaboratively in a team environment and autonomously to deliver results within specified timeframes. Contribute to a range of diagnostic skills relevant to the laboratory.
  • Exhibit initiative, problem-solving skills, and analytical abilities, including the capacity to apply established principles in a pathology laboratory and investigate and resolve general and complex issues within the laboratory environment.
  • Possess a sound understanding of legislation, policies, and requirements impacting the laboratory environment, including work health and safety and privacy requirements.
 
Skills and Requirements

  • Fully Registered Medical Practitioner with the Australian Medical Board.
  • At least 2 years full-time clinical posts following graduation from the MBBS program.
  • Demonstrated ability to consistently display commitment and leadership in high-quality customer service principles.
  • Knowledge and awareness of obligations to general principles of hospital funding (eg Casemix) and maintenance of Patients Records.
  • Demonstrated ability to undertake out-of-hours shift duties, in accordance with current EBA and AMA safe hours provisions.
  • Good communication skills with patients, relatives, peers and colleagues.
  • Demonstrated ability to pursue both formal education programs and self-education.
  • Knowledge of the ethics of medical practice.
  • Demonstrate a sound basic knowledge of internal medicine and its clinical practices.
  • Knowledge of quality improvement in medical practice.
  • Knowledge of OH&S Issues and Workplace Diversity practices.

job.title: Logistics and Operational Transformation Contract
job.description:
Overall Purpose of the Engagement
The contractor will support several strategic operational improvement initiatives across our client's specialty pathology services division and broader national operations, over an initial 3 to 6 month engagement. The engagement duration could extend beyond this period should adequate opportunities present throughout the initial term.
The role combines program delivery with hands-on operational improvement — completing an established DIFOT improvement program, rationalising logistics consumables, supporting an offshore customer service transition, shaping the service model for a new national skin laboratory, and identifying further process improvement and efficiency opportunities as they arise.
Primary Focus Areas and Responsibilities
DIFOT Improvement Program
  • Drive completion of the current DIFOT (Delivery In Full, On Time) improvement program.
  • Embed the measurement, reporting and root-cause disciplines required to sustain performance gains beyond the engagement.
Logistics Consumables Rationalisation
  • Lead a consumables rationalisation project across the specialty services environment.
  • Identify opportunities to standardise and integrate specialty consumable procurement and inventory management with the wider group's existing warehouse capabilities and buying power.
Offshore Transition
  • Support a small offshore transition initiative, aligning specialty customer service activities with the group's existing operating model.
  • Work towards consolidating in-scope service functions within the group's established contact centre in Malaysia.
National Initiative
  • Help define and execute the service model as the new national initiative takes shape.
Process Improvement and Operational Efficiency
  • Identify and deliver additional process improvement and operational efficiency opportunities within the specialty services environment.
  • Contribute to the organisation's future focus on automation and AI-driven operational improvement.
Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)
  • DIFOT performance improvement against agreed targets
  • Delivery of the consumables rationalisation project and associated savings
  • Successful transition of in-scope customer service functions to the offshore operating model
  • An agreed and executable service model for the national skin laboratory
  • Additional efficiency opportunities identified, quantified and delivered
  • Stakeholder satisfaction and engagement
THE PERSON
  • Strong logistics and supply chain experience within operationally complex organisations.
  • Demonstrated success delivering operational transformation programs.
  • Experience in automation, process excellence, continuous improvement or Lean methodologies.
  • Exposure to AI-enabled business improvement initiatives and project delivery.
  • Experience within pathology or healthcare is advantageous, although not essential.
Qualifications and Experience
  • Tertiary qualification in Supply Chain, Logistics, Business, Engineering or a related discipline, or equivalent experience.
  • A track record of delivering operational transformation and improvement programs from strategy through to execution.
  • Experience across procurement, inventory management, warehousing and distribution.
  • Familiarity with Lean, Six Sigma or comparable process excellence methodologies.
  • Strong stakeholder management and change management capabilities.
  • Well-developed written and oral communication skills.
Key Competencies
  • Strategic thinking combined with hands-on delivery
  • Program and project management
  • Process excellence and continuous improvement
  • Analytical and solutions focused
  • Stakeholder management and influencing
  • Change management
  • Commercial acumen
  • Delivery of results
  • Adaptability and pace
  • Communication and presentation skills
Engagement Terms
  • An initial engagement of 3 to 6 months, with scope to extend should adequate opportunities present during the initial term.
  • Melbourne based, working across the specialty services and broader group operations.
  • Contract rate to be determined, commensurate with experience.
job.salary: up to $1,000 per day depending upon expereince

job.title: Anatomical Pathologist - NZ
job.description:
Anatomical Pathologist
Christchurch, New Zealand | Confidential Client
Our client — a leading pathology services provider — is seeking an Anatomical Pathologist to join its Christchurch laboratory. This is a genuine opportunity to shape laboratory practice, lead quality and process improvement, and deliver diagnostic excellence within a well-resourced, collaborative environment in one of New Zealand's most liveable cities.
The Role
You will take responsibility for overseeing key operational laboratory activities, including:
  • Coordinating and delivering scientific and technical training across the laboratory team.
  • Continuously reviewing and developing laboratory practices, and driving continuous process improvement.
  •  Ensuring adherence to operational standards, procedures, and quality frameworks.
  • Contributing a broad range of diagnostic skills relevant to the laboratory.
  • Investigating and resolving general and complex issues within the laboratory environment.
About You
  • Fully registered Medical Practitioner — Medical Council of New Zealand registration, or current AMC/AHPRA registration with eligibility to register in New Zealand.

Why Christchurch?
World-class lifestyle, easy commutes, the Southern Alps and Canterbury coastline on your doorstep — and a health sector investing heavily in pathology capability.
Apply in Confidence

job.title: Business Analyst
job.description:
Business Analyst
Up to $135,000 + Super
Melbourne based | National Role
Our client is a significant and well-regarded organisation in the Australian health sector. With a broad operational footprint and a strong commitment to clinical excellence, they are a trusted provider of healthcare services supporting doctors, specialists, hospitals, and patients across the country.

Who They Are
This organisation has built a strong reputation for patient focus and medical quality. Their culture values integrity, collaboration, and continuous improvement, and they are committed to empowering their people to drive meaningful outcomes. They are currently seeking a Business Analyst to transform complex business, financial and operational data into meaningful insights that support strategic and operational decision-making across the organisation.

The Role
Reporting to the Director of Marketing, the Business Analyst combines strong technical analytical capability with commercial acumen to identify trends, opportunities and risks, enabling data-driven decision-making that enhances business performance. Working closely with Finance, Marketing and operational stakeholders, you will develop and maintain reporting solutions, support budgeting and forecasting activities, and ensure the integrity and reliability of organisational data.

This is a highly visible role where your work will directly influence business outcomes, with direct access to senior leaders across the organisation.

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

Data Analysis and Business Insights
  •  Analyse large and complex datasets to identify trends, performance drivers, risks and opportunities
  • Generate actionable insights that support commercial, financial and operational decision-making
  • Conduct detailed analysis of business performance indicators and provide recommendations for improvement
  • Present findings, trends and recommendations in a clear and concise manner to stakeholders at all levels

Reporting and Dashboard Development
  • Develop, maintain and enhance reporting dashboards using Cognos and Microsoft Excel
  • Produce regular, ad hoc and executive reporting packs with a high degree of accuracy and timeliness

Financial Planning and Performance Analysis
  • Support budgeting, forecasting and scenario modelling activities through TM1 / IBM Planning Analytics
  • Analyse key financial and operational metrics including revenue, pricing, sales volumes, margins and cost performance
  • Partner with Finance and business leaders to understand performance outcomes and identify improvement opportunities
  • Assist in developing analytical models that support strategic planning and business growth initiative

Continuous Improvement
  • Contribute to ongoing enhancements in business intelligence, reporting and performance measurement frameworks
  • Support business improvement and transformation projects across the organisation
  • Partner with stakeholders to improve business processes and support a culture of data-driven decision-making


Your Profile
You are a commercially minded analyst who enjoys solving complex business problems, uncovering insights, and driving improvement across a national organisation. You are equally comfortable working with large datasets and presenting clear, actionable recommendations to non-technical audiences.

Candidates may come from a range of backgrounds including:
  • Business analysis, data analysis, commercial analysis or financial analysis roles
  • Finance transformation, business improvement or process redesign environments
  • Healthcare, pathology, diagnostics or similarly data-driven regulated industries

You will demonstrate:
  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, Accounting, Economics, Statistics, Data Analytics, Information Systems or related discipline
  • Minimum 3–7 years' experience as a Business Analyst, Data Analyst, Commercial Analyst or similar
  • Advanced Microsoft Excel capability including Power Query, pivot tables and data modelling of large datasets
  • Experience with Cognos reporting and dashboard development
  • Experience using TM1 / IBM Planning Analytics for budgeting, forecasting and financial modelling
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and communication skills with the ability to translate complex data for non-technical audiences
  • Commercially focused with an outcomes-driven mindset

SQL or Power BI skills are a bonus, as is experience with data warehousing, ETL processes or advanced analytics tools. Experience in finance transformation or business improvement is highly regarded.


Diversity and Inclusion
Our client is an equal opportunities employer. They encourage applications from people of all ages, nationalities, abilities, and cultures — including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, the LGBTQI+ community, people living with disability, and individuals with culturally diverse backgrounds. They are happy to adjust their recruitment process to support accessibility needs.

Please note, only shortlisted applicants will be contacted, and all applicants must have a legal right to work in Australia.

You may be required to undergo probity checks as part of the recruitment process, including police checks.

For a confidential discussion or to request an information pack, please call Steve Hockey, Director at Predictus Search on 0452 525 547 or 02 8067 8521, or email your current resume with a covering letter and remuneration details to steve@predictussearch.com quoting reference A000466.

job.title: Regional Manager
job.description:
SunDoctors is Australia’s leading specialist skin cancer network, dedicated exclusively to the detection, diagnosis, and treatment of skin cancer. With over 350,000 patients seen each year and involvement in the diagnosis of almost 20% of all melanomas nationwide, SunDoctors is a purpose-driven organisation at the forefront of delivering life-saving care.
 
We are partnering with Predictus Search to appoint a Regional Manager — a pivotal operational leadership role accountable for the performance and growth of a network of SunDoctors clinics within an assigned region. This is a hands-on, high-impact position that blends commercial leadership with a genuine commitment to patient outcomes, clinical excellence, and team development.
 
This role offers the opportunity to lead an established network while also playing a key role in expansion, including the onboarding and integration of newly acquired clinics — ensuring consistent standards, strong culture alignment, and operational success from day one.
 
The Opportunity

  • Lead the financial and operational performance of clinics within your assigned region, taking ownership of the regional P&L including budgeting, forecasting, and performance optimisation.
  • Drive patient access and revenue growth through effective rostering, consulting room utilisation, and resource planning to meet demand across clinics.
  • Inspire, coach, and develop Practice Managers, building high-performing teams through structured onboarding, performance management, and succession planning.
  • Establish trusted, collaborative relationships with doctors across the region, acting as a key escalation point and partnering with recruitment teams to attract and retain top clinical talent.
  • Support network growth by leading the onboarding and integration of newly acquired clinics, ensuring seamless transitions, strong team engagement, and alignment with SunDoctors’ operating standards.
  • Champion exceptional patient experience, ensuring feedback and complaints are addressed promptly and that every clinic delivers consistently high-quality care.
  • Ensure clinics meet RACGP, ISO, and all relevant compliance and accreditation requirements, maintaining audit readiness and implementing continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Identify growth opportunities, strengthen referral pathways, and build strategic external partnerships to support regional expansion.
  • Promote and integrate Southern Sun Pathology services across clinics to enhance patient outcomes and service delivery.
 
About You

  • A proven leader with the ability to build, inspire, and develop high-performing clinical and administrative teams.
  • Minimum 5 years’ experience in healthcare, clinical services, or multi-site operational leadership.
  • Strong commercial acumen with demonstrated experience managing P&L, budgets, and financial performance.
  • Sound understanding of compliance and accreditation standards (RACGP, ISO, WHS).
  • A confident communicator with the ability to engage effectively with doctors, frontline teams, and senior stakeholders.
  • Highly organised and data-driven, with the ability to manage multiple priorities across geographically dispersed sites.
  • Passionate about healthcare, with a genuine commitment to patient safety, service excellence, and continuous improvement.
 
Why Join SunDoctors?

This is a unique opportunity to lead, influence, and grow a network of market-leading skin cancer clinics, while contributing to a mission that has a tangible impact on the health of Australians.
 
You will play a key role not only in operational excellence, but also in shaping the future footprint of the business through clinic expansion and acquisitions.
 
The role includes travel within the assigned region, with an expectation of being on-site across clinics approximately three to four days per week.

job.title: Anatomical Veterinary Pathologist
job.description:
Veterinary Anatomical Pathologist

​Gribbles Veterinary Pathology is a trading entity of Australian Clinical Labs and it is one of Australia’s leading Veterinary Pathology providers, with two dedicated veterinary laboratories within Australia. Each laboratory provides diagnostic pathology services for livestock, companion animal, university and research veterinarians, as well zoo and wildlife organisations.

The Opportunity

They are currently seeking an enthusiastic and dynamic Veterinary Anatomical Pathologist based at their dedicated laboratory in South Australia.
 
In this role, you will provide timely diagnostic pathology services, including postmortem examinations, cytology, and histopathology, and contribute to the provision of services and advice to PIRSA. The scope of pathology work at this laboratory is wide and is a true mix of both large and small animal pathology, and of both anatomical and clinical pathology.
 
Your Key Responsibilities
 
  • Interpretation of both anatomical (gross post-mortem, histopathology) and clinical pathology results
  • This includes evaluation and interpretation of haematology, cytology, biochemistry, endocrinology, urinalysis, serology, microbiology & molecular results
  • Complete post-mortem exams on small and large animals
  • Oversee preparation of tissue for testing 
  • Participation in the provision of services and advice to PIRSA
  • Provision of specialist advice and phone consultation to veterinary clients
  • Provide scientific leadership to the laboratory technical team through mentorship, audits, and assistance with laboratory electronic records management and reporting systems in accordance to NATA accreditation.
  • Provide support to the Commercial team to consistently understand and meet the needs of our clients and participation in marketing activities to meet professional expectations.
  • Cooperate and work well with others in pursuit of team goals
 
Essential requirements

  • Degree in Veterinary Science (BVSc) or equivalent.
  • Registration as a veterinarian with the Veterinary Practitioners Board in Australia.
  • Pathology qualification by examination, (e.g. ACVP, ECVP, MANZCVS) or equivalent diagnostic pathology experience in production animals.
  • Post Graduate qualification in veterinary pathology or related discipline is preferred.
  • Experience in clinical veterinary pathology would be desirable, and a demonstrated commitment to providing a high-quality pathology service.

​
Our supportive professional environment also provides opportunities for further career development through continuing professional education development and active participation in continuing education seminars for clients.

Salary is commensurate with experience and qualifications

job.title: Clinical Veterinary Pathologist
job.description:
Full Time/Part Time/Remote Clinical Veterinary Pathologist 
                         
Gribbles Veterinary Pathology is a trading entity of Australian Clinical Labs and it is one of Australia’s leading Veterinary Pathology providers, with two dedicated veterinary laboratories within Australia. Each laboratory provides diagnostic pathology services for livestock, companion animal, university, and research veterinarians, as well zoo and wildlife organisations.
 
About the Opportunity
 
We are currently seeking an enthusiastic and dynamic Veterinary Clinical Pathologist with a client-oriented approach and excellent communication skills on a full-time or part-time basis, either 2-3 full days or a few hours each morning over 5 days.
 
In this role, you will provide timely diagnostic pathology services, including postmortem examinations, cytology, and haematology, and contribute to the provision of services and advice to a broad range of clients. The scope of pathology work at this laboratory is wide and is a true mix of both large and small animal pathology, and of both anatomical and clinical pathology.
 
Your Key Responsibilities
 
  • Interpretation of both anatomical (gross post mortem, histopathology) and clinical pathology results
  • This includes evaluation and interpretation of haematology, cytology, biochemistry, endocrinology, urinalysis, serology, microbiology & molecular results
  • Reviewing haematology and chemistry data, interpreting cytology, consulting on case management, liaising with clinicians
  • Provision of specialist advice and phone consultation to veterinary clients
  • Provide scientific leadership to the laboratory technical team through mentorship, audits, and assistance with laboratory electronic records management and reporting systems in accordance to NATA accreditation.
  • Provide support to the Commercial team to consistently understand and meet the needs of our clients and participation in marketing activities to meet professional expectations.
  • Cooperate and work well with others in pursuit of team goals
 
 
Essential requirements
 
  • Degree in Veterinary Science (BVSc) or equivalent.
  • Registration as a veterinarian with the Veterinary Practitioners Board in Australia.
  • Pathology qualification by examination, (e.g. ACVP, ECVP, MANZCVS) or equivalent diagnostic pathology experience in production animals.
  • Post Graduate qualification in veterinary pathology or related discipline is preferred.
  • Experience in clinical veterinary pathology is essential, and a demonstrated commitment to providing a high quality pathology service.
  • Quantitative analysis, data interpretation, cytology, clinical reasoning, correlating lab data with patient signs.
 
Our supportive professional environment also provides opportunities for further career development through continuing professional education development and active participation in continuing education seminars for clients.
 
Salary is commensurate with experience and qualifications.

job.title: Head of Anatomical Pathology
job.description:
Head of Anatomical Pathology
 
The Anatomic Pathology Laboratory Manager plan, organize, and direct the overall operation of the Anatomical Pathology Laboratory. Assist with budget preparation, monitoring of revenue, expenses, test volume, FTE utilization, report/result turnaround, as well as workflow, and customer/employee satisfaction; plan and manage technology innovations, new facility design and implementation, new business, laboratory expansion, focus on service, maintains compliance with State, Federal, CAP and other accreditation agencies' regulations, in adherence to departmental and company policies and procedures and promote the company's mission and values across the integrated laboratory network. Expected to participate in the Senior Leadership Team, coordinate AP Lab departments involved in initiatives, and help develop the strategic direction for the AP operations.
 
Key objectives:

Clinical oversight - Work across the geographical scope of the Laboratory, performing or supervising anatomical pathology services consistent with the pathologist’s scope of training and registration, and other diagnostic collection techniques, reporting cases, and conducting clinical meetings and case discussions.
Clinical Governance - Participate in all clinical governance activities, including clinical audit, clinical effectiveness, risk management, quality assurance and quality improvement activities.
Capacity building - Provide leadership to promote the interest and development of the unit through strategic planning, ensuring cohesion of the overall functions of the unit by working effectively with internal and external stakeholders while always maintaining positive interpersonal relationships.
Health and Safety and Infection Control - Ensure that all duties and responsibilities of this post are carried out in compliance with the local work health and safety requirements, but also to Australian standards.
 
Responsibilities

  • Collaborates with Anatomic Laboratory Director, Laboratory Medical Director, Laboratory Leadership, and other AP Laboratory staff to suggest test methodologies and instrumentation appropriate for clinical use.
  • Participate in the hiring, training, and promotion of laboratory staff in conjunction with Laboratory Leadership.
  • Grow and develop staff to increase overall knowledge base.
  • Create a culture of operational and continuous quality improvement.
  • Manages conflict and identifies problems to arrive at constructive solutions while maintaining positive working relationships.
  • Involved with the selection, validation, and implementation of new test platforms.
  • Oversees the technical and operational aspects of the Laboratory.
  • Supports the development and delivery of laboratory service collaterals.
  • Communicates to Management updates of departmental action items on a regular basis.
  • Ensures compliance with all applicable Federal, State, CAP, and other accreditation agencies' regulations.
  • Establishes and implements metrics, policies, objectives, and procedures for departments and reports on results and outcomes.
  • Ensures that CQI efforts in conjunction with the Quality Officer comply with regulatory and accreditation standards.
  • Coordinates, supports, and monitors laboratory departments with a major focus on improving the operations to run seamlessly to ensure quality patient care.
  • Assists in the development of budgets including recommendations for major equipment purchases.
  • Assists in the development of facility designs and remodels.
  • Develop and implement strategic plans in alignment with the company's values and mission.
  • Performs other related duties as assigned.
 
Selection criteria:
﻿
Essential Skills, Experience and Knowledge Qualifications
  • Candidates must have qualifications suitable for registration as a medical practitioner (such as a medical degree from an Australian institution)
  • Eligible for Medical registration with the Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (AHPRA) or equivalent
  • Post-graduate speciality qualifications in general pathology, including anatomical pathology and microbiology, recognised by the Royal College of Pathologists (Australasia)
  • Anatomical/surgical pathologist is most preferred, but the clinical/general pathologist is considered as well.
  • Bachelor's Degree in Histotechnology, Cytotechnology, other science-related field, or equivalent; Master's degree preferred
  • HT/HTL, PA, CT ASCP certification required or equivalent.
  • 5 years experience in the laboratory, a similar environment
  • Three (3) or more years of supervisory experience, preferred.
  • Knowledge of Quality Improvement programs, processes, and tools
  • Ability to work with individuals at all organizational levels, particularly peers, team members, Pathologists, and other departments.
  • Knowledge of project planning, budgeting, human resources management, and report development
  • Prior experience validating and implementing new Excellent analytical, organizational, communication, interpersonal and public speaking Self-directed, open to new learning experiences and demonstrating teamwork.
  • Ability to coordinate multiple resources effectively to accomplish a task or accept an idea through leadership.
  • High level of competency with computers, the internet, and computer software such as MS Office (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint)
